finding.title: Provider review ask does not re-ask for remaining paired-device changes; step fails instead
finding.scenario: A workstation Mission (envelope granted by the workstation) has a model step with access write. Paired-device Missions have already left 13 unreviewed project changes (two phone-approved Missions of 7 and 6 bounded filesystem.write steps; Plan limit is 12 steps per Mission). The model step's dispatch raises a provider.execute review ask (dispatch branch, reviewViolation, lines ~1432-1443) whose remoteReview holds the 12 shown ids and whose reason says '1 more changed file(s) are listed for review after these'. The workstation answers allow_once. handleAnswer acknowledges the 12 shown ids (line 3616) and then calls this.tasks.approve(step.taskId, by) (line 3678). launch() re-runs missionScopeCheck, and the review check at line 105 still sees 1 pending change, so the launch is refused. The catch at ~3679-3690 marks the step failed as provider_unavailable and does not raise a new ask. Result: the second page is never shown, the Mission goes to waiting_for_user, and the user must Retry to see the remaining change. This contradicts the round-5 requirement (A) that remaining changes ask again after the answer. No code ran (fail-closed), but the failure is misleading.
finding.evidence: Probe (throwaway, own temp folder, since deleted) drove MissionManager with the real TaskManager and a fake claude adapter. Output: 'pending remote changes: 13'; 'ask1 remoteReview: 12 reason tail: ... 1 more changed file(s) are listed for review after these; review them before allowing'; after answer: 'launched= 0 missionState= waiting_for_user stepState= failed stepFailure= {category: provider_unavailable, detail: Outside mission execution scope: Approval required on Windows Host ... Files were changed under paired-device authorit...}'; 'open asks after answer: 0 pendingRemoteChanges: 1'. Contrast: the capability path (bus.server.ts re-runs the capability in the same step) does page correctly, and test F01-R31 covers only that path. Relevant code: manager.server.ts:105 (missionScopeCheck review check), :1432-1443 (dispatch review ask), :3616 (ack), :3678 (approve on answer), and the approve catch block that calls stepFailed.
finding.recommendation: On the provider.execute answer path, after tasks.approve, detect a remaining pending review (pendingRemoteReview() non-null) and re-issue the provider.execute ask via askPermission with the new remoteReview ids and desktopRequired, the same way the DesktopRequestStale branch does, instead of failing the step. Or make approve-time refusal for pending review a re-ask. Add a test mirroring F01-R31 for provider.execute with 13 pending changes that asserts a second ask and launched === 0 until both pages are answered.

votes.reasoning:
The defect is real but is a correctness/UX gap, not a security boundary crossing, so I rate it LOW rather than MEDIUM.

Verified by reading the code (no probe run, no repo files touched):
- manager.server.ts:2289-2296 pendingRemoteReview() pages paths (REVIEW_PAGE) and returns more = remaining count. The dispatch ask at :1432-1443 sends the 12 shown ids plus the "more" text.
- handleAnswer, :3602-3616: on allow_once by a trusted-local actor with remoteReview, store.acknowledgeRemoteChanges acknowledges only the shown ids. The remaining change stays pending.
- :3678 calls this.tasks.approve(step.taskId, by). Host manager.server.ts:1046-1050 runs missionScopeCheck(task) in the default "check" phase before any state change. Mission manager :105 then refuses because pendingRemoteReview() is still non-null for a shell-capable provider session. The error is rethrown as "Outside mission execution scope".
- The catch at :3679-3690 calls stepFailed(provider_unavailable). No new askPermission is raised on this path. Compare the DesktopRequestStale branch at :3600-3610, which does re-ask. The capability path re-pages, which is what F01-R31 tests, so the provider path is the gap.

Why it is not a security issue: the refusal is fail-closed, so nothing runs over unreviewed changes. No authority is expanded, and the second page only has to be shown through a Retry. Still, round-5 requirement (A) says remaining changes ask again after the answer, and this path does not do that, so it is a legitimate defect and not refutable. The proposed fix (re-issue provider.execute ask when pendingRemoteReview() is non-null after approve, and add an F01-R31-style provider test) is sensible. I did not verify that Retry re-raises the ask, which the finding also assumes.

The finding's mechanics hold on the code I read, so I did not refute it. Its severity is overstated.

Confirmed path:
- src/lib/bunny-missions/manager.server.ts:1432-1433 raises reviewViolation whenever pendingRemoteReview() is non-null for a shell-capable session. The ask at 1442-1452 carries remoteReview (the 12 shown ids) and desktopRequired.
- handleAnswer acknowledges only request.remoteReview (3615-3617), so the 13th change stays pending.
- The only re-ask in handleAnswer is the DesktopRequestStale catch (3599-3607). On the provider.execute path, after the answer, control reaches this.tasks.approve(step.taskId, by) at 3678 with no re-ask.
- src/lib/bunny-host/manager.server.ts:1047-1049 (approve's check phase) calls missionScopeCheck(task) and throws "Outside mission execution scope" when it returns a string. The review check at manager.server.ts:105 returns that string while one change is pending. The catch at 3679-3691 then fails the step as provider_unavailable.
- The existing F01-R31 test covers only the capability (terminal.exec) path. No provider.execute equivalent exists.

Why it is not higher than LOW:
- Fail-closed. No code runs, no authority is expanded, and the minted desktop grant is revoked in the catch.
- The defect is an availability and UX gap against round-5 requirement (A) ("remaining changes ask again after that answer"). It is not a security boundary crossing.
- It is not one of the listed dispositions or accepted limitations. It is a real deviation from the stated requirement, so it is not refuted.

Repo files were not modified. No repo tests were run beyond the permitted one, and I created no temp files. I did not re-run the probe; the reported probe output is consistent with the code I read.

finding.title: Workstation-approved session descendants escape the mid-run hold and review gate once the session ends
finding.scenario: A workstation allow_once approves a shell-capable provider session (Claude write or Codex). The session starts a detached background process that imports project modules later (dev server, watcher, or any long-lived child). The session finishes: TaskManager's finally deletes tasks.sessions (src/lib/bunny-host/manager.server.ts:1637), and the bus removes bus.liveCode (src/lib/bunny-missions/capabilities/bus.server.ts:348). liveCodeExecutions() (manager.server.ts:2298-2306) then reports nothing live, so remoteMutationHeld() returns null. A paired device approves a filesystem.write over the module the surviving process imports. The write lands and is recorded as pending, but no hold applies, and no new code run is asked, because the code already running is not a new run. The background process then executes the device-authored content. Probe (fake claude adapter whose launch spawns a detached node child that imports ./helper.mjs after 3 s): after the workstation-approved session completed (tasks.sessions 0, bus.liveCode 0, liveCodeExecutions []), the phone-approved write completed with zero requests on the mission, and the background process printed DEVICE-AUTHORED. Control: the same pattern under terminal.exec does not reproduce, because runWindowsOwnedProcess/OwnedProcessGroup.close kills the job; the detached child never wrote its output. Mitigating caveats: whether a real provider leaves descendants alive is agent- and platform-dependent; the Host's stopTree (src/lib/bunny-host/manager.server.ts:1691-1695) only clears the process-tree timer and does not kill anything, and terminate() in src/lib/bunny-host/adapters.server.ts:195-200 runs only on fail or user stop. Liveness is also in-memory (bus.liveCode is a plain Map, bus.server.ts:106; desktopExecutions likewise), so after a Host restart surviving workstation-approved processes are invisible to the hold, which is the same gap.
finding.evidence: Probe run in a throwaway temp folder (deleted). Output: 'ask: provider.execute true'; 'coder mission: completed | tasks.sessions: 0 | bus.liveCode: 0 | liveCodeExecutions: []'; 'device edit: completed | held? requests: 0 | pending review: true'; 'background process output: DEVICE-AUTHORED at ...'. Terminal control: 'run done ... liveCode 0', device edit completed, ran2 absent while the heartbeat file existed. Relevant lines: manager.server.ts:2298 (liveCodeExecutions), :2317 (remoteMutationHeld), bus.server.ts:348 (liveCode.delete in finally), host manager.server.ts:1637 and :1691.
finding.recommendation: Do not drop liveness when the root process or session ends while descendants may still run. Options: (1) at session end, kill the session's process tree (taskkill /T on the recorded pid, or move provider sessions into an owned group like terminal.exec) and confirm no survivors before clearing liveness; (2) keep liveness while any descendant in the last processTree snapshot is alive; (3) persist live-code records across Host restart and hold device-attributable mutations until the workstation confirms no survivors. Add a regression test where the fake session spawns a detached child that imports a device-changed module.

votes.reasoning:
Not refuted. Code reading confirms the gap. liveCodeExecutions() (src/lib/bunny-missions/manager.server.ts:2298-2306) counts only tasks.sessions keys and bus.liveCode entries. The session entry is removed in the finally block at src/lib/bunny-host/manager.server.ts:1637, which runs on normal completion after the adapter's done promise resolves. bus.liveCode is cleared at bus.server.ts:348. The only process-survivor cleanup, the killProcess/survivors loop at manager.server.ts:1724-1748, runs only on user stop (stop()). stopTree (line 1691) clears only the observation timer. terminate() in adapters.server.ts:195-200 runs only on fail() or a user stop. So a workstation-approved session whose detached descendant outlives it leaves no liveness record, remoteMutationHeld() returns null, and a paired device write over a module that the survivor later imports is admitted without a hold or new review gate.

Precondition checked: the session's done promise resolves on the child 'close' event (adapters.server.ts ~line 230), not on 'exit'. I probed Node semantics in a mkdtemp folder (deleted). A grandchild that inherits the parent's stdout/stderr pipe delays 'close' until it exits (about 4 s in the probe). A grandchild with stdio ignored, or with output redirected to a file, lets 'close' fire immediately. So the bug reproduces only when the surviving descendant detaches its stdout/stderr. That is a common daemon/watcher pattern (for example, a shell redirect like `cmd > log 2>&1 &`), so it is realistic but conditional. I did not re-run the full fake-adapter probe; I relied on the code path and the stdio probe.

Severity: HIGH is what I'd assign. The device-authored content would execute through a process the workstation approved, which is close to the BLOCKER definition, but it requires a specific surviving-descendant shape. The owner-policy dispositions and accepted limitations listed do not cover this case: the in-memory liveness limitation is listed only as an extension of the same gap, and it does not excuse an in-session gap.

Not refuted. I re-read the code paths by reading only; I did not re-run the probe and made no repo edits.

Liveness drops at session end, as claimed:
- manager.server.ts:2298-2306 liveCodeExecutions() reports only tasks.sessions entries and bus.liveCode values. Neither tracks descendants.
- host manager.server.ts:1632-1638 finally runs stopTree, flushers.delete and sessions.delete. Nothing kills the tree.
- bus.server.ts:348 finally runs liveCode.delete(base.id) for capability runs. The session path does not use bus.liveCode, but the Host-side liveness has the same gap.
- stopTree (host manager.server.ts ~1691-1695) only clears the timer.
- adapters.server.ts spawnSession: done resolves on child 'close'. Nothing calls terminate() on normal completion. terminate() runs only on fail or stop, plus the runtime-limit path via stopInBackground.
- owned-processes.server.ts trackOwnedChild on 'close' only releases the handle from the owned Set. It does not kill anything. stopOwnedChildren runs only at Host shutdown.

So after the root child closes, nothing ties a surviving descendant to liveness. remoteMutationHeld (manager.server.ts:2309-2320) then returns null for a device write. Nothing else gates it either: pendingRemoteReview covers only new runsCode/shell-session launches, and the desktopExecutions "task:" entry (manager.server.ts:116) uses live = task non-terminal, which is also false after completion.

The gap contradicts the stated round-4 intent of holding device mutations while workstation-approved code is live. A detached survivor is that code.

Caveats I weighed: real providers may not leave survivors. The write must be an in-envelope planned step, and the survivor must re-read that file. Those preconditions keep this from BLOCKER. I did not find a disposition or accepted limitation that covers it: the listed "mid-run hold" and "review gate" items are about live runs, not about survivors after the session record is gone. Severity stays HIGH, consistent with the finding.

Related scope note: the same post-end drop applies to any workstation-approved runsCode capability whose launched child outlives the capability (bus.server.ts:348), if such a capability is classified as runsCode.

finding.title: browser.download recorded as a project change at the mission folder path, so the review prompt names the wrong item
finding.scenario: remoteMutationStarted records path = request.cwd when params.path is not a string (manager.server.ts:163). browser.download has only url/selector params, so the pending change is the mission folder. The workstation prompt built from remoteChanges() (manager.server.ts:2268-2274, which uses run.params.path ?? run.action) reads 'Files changed ... : browser.download'. The downloaded file lands under the Host artifacts folder, not the project. The review is still Host-wide, so no code run bypasses it; the prompt just does not name the file the workstation should review.
finding.evidence: Code reading only (not probed). Lines: manager.server.ts:160-166 (bus.remoteMutationStarted), :163 (path fallback), :2268-2274 (remoteChanges), bus.server.ts:306 (remoteMutationStarted call before adapter execution). browser.download writes to dataDirectory/artifacts per browser.server.ts:238.
finding.recommendation: Record the downloaded file path from the run output (output.path) for browser.download, and show that path in both the pending review rows and the prompt text.

finding.title: Folder-conflict asks are answerable by a paired device but never execute while the blocking run is live, and re-ask at once
finding.scenario: While a trusted-desktop execution runs in a folder, bus.decision() returns {decision:'ask', reason:'A trusted-desktop execution is running in this folder...'} for any Mission mutation there (bus.server.ts:162-163), without desktopRequired. deviceRequestRefusal() does not refuse it, so a phone can answer allow_once. Each answer is consumed and the same ask reappears immediately while the run lives. After the run ends, the write still needs another answer, and the mission stays waiting_for_user with the filesystem.write ask open. No write executes while the run is live, so this is not a bypass. It is a wedge/looping issue for benign flows (a remote mission whose own run is live in its folder). Probe: three phone allow_once answers, each followed by a new identical ask; out.txt not written; run still live; the mission stayed waiting_for_user after the run ended.
finding.evidence: Probe output: 'write asks: filesystem.write desktopRequired=false ... reason="A trusted-desktop execution is running in this folder; this change waits until it finishes"' (x3); 'write requests total: 4 | run still live: 1 | write mission state: waiting_for_user | out.txt: false'; after run end 'state waiting_for_user | open requests: [ filesystem.write ]'. Code: bus.server.ts:162-163; manager.server.ts desktopExecutionStarted/desktopExecutionConflict (around lines 2250-2265 region of the desktop-grant helpers).
finding.recommendation: Either resume the held step automatically when the conflicting execution ends, or mark this ask as not answerable by a device with an explicit reason, so phone answers are not accepted and discarded. Optional: give the workstation a clear 'waits for run X' state instead of a re-ask.

finding.title: Workstation-authority Git reads run repo/config textconv and clean filters outside the review gate
finding.scenario: A Mission under a workstation envelope has a planned bounded write (device-approved one-time or accepted as an ordinary in-envelope write) that creates a repo script S (not a config path, so remoteExecutionRefusal allows it). The repo's committed .gitattributes maps a path to diff=x, and the owner's git config defines diff.x.textconv = "node S". The verification check git_diff_nonempty runs git.diff as READ, so runsCode() returns false and the Host-wide pendingRemoteChanges review gate never asks. GitCapability.git() only adds --no-textconv/--no-ext-diff/hook-disable flags when context.remoteAuthority is set, so the device-written script S executes on the workstation's own verification without any review. The same unhardened path lets a configured clean filter run on git.status (probed: runs under both remote and workstation authority, so the clean-filter part overlaps the accepted limitation; the textconv part is only blocked for remote authority).
finding.evidence: Probe (temp repo under OS temp, deleted afterwards): repo with .gitattributes '*.txt diff=x', config diff.x.textconv='node conv.js', conv.js writes a marker. GitCapability(data).execute('git.diff', {cwd}, ctx) with remoteAuthority=false -> status succeeded, marker present. With remoteAuthority=true -> status succeeded, marker absent. Clean-filter probe with git.status: marker present under both. runsCode at src/lib/bunny-missions/authorization.server.ts:218-220 covers only terminal.exec, GIT_MUTATIONS and non-Calculator EXECUTE; bus gate at src/lib/bunny-missions/capabilities/bus.server.ts (review = runsCode(...) ? remoteReviewFor) therefore skips git.diff/git.status. Precondition: owner-configured textconv or filter whose command runs a repo-relative file; not reachable from default config.
finding.recommendation: Treat any Git invocation that can spawn configured programs (diff, status, log, show, and any unhardened call) as code-running for the review gate, or harden every Mission-scoped git call (--no-textconv, --no-ext-diff, filter/fsmonitor overrides via -c) regardless of envelope authority; add a probe test that a textconv pointing at a device-written script is refused or reviewed.

finding.title: Single Calculator computer actions match windows by substring title, not the exact Calculator window
finding.scenario: A paired device may approve computer.invoke_control or computer.focus_window only when remoteCalculatorOperation passes, which requires params.title === 'Calculator' exactly (authorization.server.ts:159-161). But on the non-batch path (no desktopBatch, i.e. every single device answer), Find-Window selects the first top-level window whose Name is -like '*Calculator*' (line 75), and invoke_control (lines 337-340) and focus_window (lines 308-313) run Assert-BatchControl/Assert-BatchWindow only when a batch is present. So an exact reviewed op 'invoke num5Button in Calculator' or 'focus Calculator' can act on any other window whose title merely contains 'Calculator' (for example 'Calculator - Google Chrome' or a notes window), and the Calculator native-frame identity check never runs.
finding.evidence: PowerShell check on this machine: 'Calculator - Google Chrome','Calculator' -like '*Calculator*' returns both values, so the wildcard matches a non-Calculator window. Find-Window at computer.server.ts:57-76, wildcard at line 75 (the $batch branch at 63-72 is the only one with exact Name -ne title and Native-CalculatorFrame). remoteCalculatorOperation at authorization.server.ts:159-161 and the device gate at authorization.server.ts:207 accept title 'Calculator' with no runtime identity check. Impact is UI automation on another window (focus, or invoke of Calculator automation IDs), not code execution; the live Windows UI was not exercised.
finding.recommendation: For any Calculator-bound op, match exact Name equality (and the Native-CalculatorFrame owner check) in the single path too, or refuse title-based device operations and require a pid/window handle that the Host verified as calc.exe at ask time.

finding.title: Provider review answer fails the step instead of re-asking when more than 12 device changes are pending
finding.scenario: Round-5 fix (A) is not met on the provider.execute path. A Mission has 13 unreviewed paired-device changes. A workstation-approved Claude write step asks provider.execute with remoteReview of 12 ids. The workstation answers allow_once. respond() acknowledges the 12 ids, then calls tasks.approve(). launch() runs missionScopeCheck (check phase, line 105), which sees the 13th pending change and refuses with DESKTOP_REQUIRED. The refusal is caught at lines 3678-3692 and the step is failed with category provider_unavailable. No session launches, and no new ask is raised for the remaining change. Nothing executes, so this is fail-closed, but the step is mislabelled and needs a Retry. The capability path (bus review ask, test F01-R31) does re-ask correctly.
finding.evidence: Probe in a private temp folder, built from remote-authority.test.ts setup helpers. Result: 'pending remote changes: 13'; ask desktopRequired=true remoteReview=12; after the workstation answer the step is failed with failure.category=provider_unavailable and detail 'Outside mission execution scope: Approval required on Windows Host ... Files were changed under paired-device authority and need review on the Windows Host first.'; launched sessions: 0; open requests: []; pending remote changes now: 1. Retry then raises a fresh provider.execute ask with reviewLen 1; a device answer is refused with 'Approval required on Windows Host'; the workstation answer launches the session. Relevant lines: manager.server.ts:105 (pending check in missionScopeCheck), 1432-1433 (child-creation review ask), 2289 (pendingRemoteReview), 3678 and 3689 (respond catch).
finding.recommendation: In respond()'s provider.execute branch, when tasks.approve fails because of a pending-review refusal, re-raise the review ask for the remaining paths (the same way the bus does, using pendingRemoteReview()) instead of calling stepFailed with provider_unavailable. Add a test that 13 pending changes give a second provider.execute ask, not a failed step.

votes.reasoning:
Not refuted. The defect is real, is a correctness gap against round-5 fix (A), and is fail-closed.

Code path, traced statically (I did not re-run the probe):
- manager.server.ts:1432 computes review = pendingRemoteReview(), which caps ids at REVIEW_PAGE=12 (line 73, 2294). The provider.execute ask carries remoteReview: review.ids, so the ask shows 12 ids.
- respond() (around 3615-3617) acknowledges only those 12 ids after allow_once.
- The provider.execute branch (3669-3692) calls this.tasks.approve(). That goes through launch() (host manager.server.ts ~1129), which runs missionScopeCheck(final, "check"). The check at missionScopeCheck (manager.server.ts:105-106) sees the 13th pending change and returns DESKTOP_REQUIRED.
- The throw is caught at 3674. The step is failed with "provider_unavailable" (3689) and no re-ask is raised. Nothing launches: the throw precedes the adapter call.

Impact: No device authority is extended and no code runs, so there is no security breach. The step is mislabelled and the workstation's answer is wasted. machine.ts:115 maps provider_unavailable to retry/reroute, so the mission may auto-reroute. That reroute still passes through askPermission with reviewViolation or through the launch-phase check, so the gate still holds. Test F01-R31 (remote-authority.test.ts:1150-1170) covers only the bus path, not provider.execute, which explains the gap. Severity LOW is appropriate.

finding.title: A paired device can acknowledge workstation attention entries and hide pending approvals from the workstation list
finding.scenario: inbox.ack is in the device REMOTE set and DEVICE_RIGHTS (supervise). The handler calls inbox.acknowledge(id) with no check of the entry's kind or mission. inbox.server.ts:66-70 sets acknowledgedAt, and the workstation attention list in mission.tsx:329 filters out acknowledged items. A device can therefore hide a workstation requires_approval entry for a pending desktop-only approval (for example a terminal.exec ask) while the request stays open and unanswered. This does not grant authority; it only removes an alert from the workstation UI.
finding.evidence: Probe: a remote-approved Mission with a terminal.exec step asks desktop-only. Before the device ack, the workstation attention filter returned 2 entries (requires_attention and requires_approval). The device sent inbox.ack for the requires_approval entry, which was accepted. Afterwards the filter returned 1 entry, and the request was still open with the step in waiting_for_approval. Relevant lines: commands.server.ts:27 (REMOTE includes inbox.ack), commands.server.ts:83, inbox.server.ts:66-70, mission.tsx:329.
finding.recommendation: Make device acknowledgement of requires_approval and requires_attention entries an answer-side or workstation-only action, or drop inbox.ack from REMOTE and DEVICE_RIGHTS. Alternatively keep it device-visible but have the workstation attention list keep any entry whose request is still open, regardless of acknowledgedAt.

finding.title: Device answer to a non-mutating ask resumes workstation-envelope code execution the device could not start
finding.scenario: Workstation-approved Mission (workstation envelope, not remote) with step 1 = filesystem.read seed.txt and step 2 = terminal.exec node probe.mjs (dependsOn step 1). The Mission is waiting_for_user on one pending, device-answerable READ ask for step 1 (in envelope, no config path, no mutation so no review gate). A paired device calls mission.start: refused ('a paired device cannot authorize command or code execution', commands.server.ts:60 / deviceStartRefusal). The same device calls mission.respond allow_once on the READ ask: accepted. respond() (manager.server.ts ~3562 device refusal, ~3642 waiting_for_user -> running, then setStep ready and schedule) never calls deviceStartRefusal/deviceResumeRefusal, so step 2 runs terminal.exec to completion (ran.txt written) with no workstation action. Control: the identical workstation answer produces the same result, so the device answer is the trigger. The same unguarded resume applies to verify-phase answers (verifyAndComplete runs command checks) and to allow_batch (setStep ready + schedule), and to shell-capable provider steps in such Missions (not separately probed).
finding.evidence: Throwaway probe (node --experimental-strip-types, repo modules imported by file URL, temp data dir removed afterwards). Output: scenario A device mission.start -> 'device start refused: Approval required on Windows Host: a paired device cannot authorize command or code execut...', ranFile=false. Scenario B device mission.respond allow_once on pending filesystem.read ask -> accepted, runCount [terminal.exec:succeeded, filesystem.read:succeeded], finalState completed, ranFile=true. Control C workstation respond -> identical. Round-4 contract (task text) says a device never decides when workstation-held code execution begins or resumes, and the start (commands.server.ts:60) and agent.resume (agent-runtime.server.ts ~209, deviceResumeRefusal) gates exist, but respond() has no equivalent gate. Note: when the device answer is for a mutation (filesystem.write), the Host-wide review gate instead holds the terminal step (pendingRemoteChanges), so the gap is specific to non-mutating device-answerable asks.
finding.recommendation: In respond(), for a device actor (decision !== deny), refuse with WorkstationRequiredError when the Mission's deviceStartRefusal(mission) (or, for Agents, deviceResumeRefusal) is non-null, before any resume transition, approvedOnce, or verifyAndComplete. Remote envelopes already return null from deviceStartRefusal, so remote behaviour is unchanged. Add a regression test: workstation Mission with a planned terminal step, device answers a pending in-envelope read ask -> refused, nothing runs. Consider the same gate for allow_batch and the verify-phase branch.
finding.severity_note: Severity HIGH rather than BLOCKER: the terminal step was already inside the workstation-approved envelope, so the device adds timing control, not new authority. Under the literal 'device can cause code execution' scale it could be escalated to BLOCKER by the owner.

finding.title: File-exists verification reads are not judged on device one-time answers
finding.scenario: Agent Mission step with executor filesystem.read on seed.txt (in envelope) and a verification check {kind:'file_exists', path:'C:/Windows/win.ini'}. The verify-phase ask for filesystem.read on that path is raised by the agentic check (out of Agent consent). deviceRequestRefusal builds candidates only from executor params and capability-kind verification checks (lines 2071-2073), so file_exists checks are never judged; the device answer returns null and the one-time allowance carries into the verification read. The Agent path does not re-check request.params against the Mission envelope before the device answer, and the Mission-envelope check is skipped by decide() for oneTime. Impact is limited: FilesystemCapability.read uses scopedPath with the envelope projectRoots (device answers never extend roots), so out-of-root paths still fail; in-root unconsented reads are the case the owner disposition already covers. The same capability-kind check on that path is refused (probe), so the omission is specific to file_exists.
finding.evidence: Throwaway probe calling MissionManager.prototype.deviceRequestRefusal on a fake step with a file_exists verification of C:/Windows/win.ini returned null, while the capability-kind verification of the same path returned 'Approval required on Windows Host.'; scopeViolation for that path returns 'outside the approved read scope'. Related, by code reading only (not probed): askPermission (manager.server.ts ~3374) computes the request fingerprint via agenticRequestParams(verify), which for a file_exists check falls back to the executor params, so a verify-phase ask for the check path is fingerprint-bound to the executor path. This does not grant anything (reviewedFilesystemOnce requires an exact fingerprint match), but it makes such verify asks loop or fail.
finding.recommendation: Judge every same-action check the step can reach, including file_exists (action filesystem.read or filesystem.exists with check.path) and git_diff_nonempty (git.diff), in deviceRequestRefusal's candidate list, and compare request.params to the candidate set rather than only to executor params. Fix agenticRequestParams(verify) so file_exists checks bind their own path. Add a regression test alongside F01-R32 for the file_exists kind.
